prediction.likelyOutcome: Dover Mall should win summary judgment on liability and on the pre-surrender arrears (roughly $190,000-$205,000) essentially outright, since Tang concedes both the breach and the calculation and his force majeure/frustration defenses are foreclosed by the lease's explicit rent carve-out and ordinary frustration doctrine. The accelerated/future-rent component covering the post-surrender period, however, likely survives summary judgment and heads to trial because the record contains no actual evidence of reletting efforts, giving Tang's mitigation defense real traction on that slice of the claim; net recovery is likely to land well below the full $276,089.72 requested.

issues.label: Post-Surrender Accelerated/Future Rent Through Lease End

outcome.description: The Superior Court granted the landlord summary judgment on liability and damages in the amount of $276,089.72, the full amount demanded, holding the force majeure clause allocated pandemic-closure risk to the tenant and two lease provisions relieved the landlord of any duty to relet. No attorney's fee award is stated. This is a trial-level decision; no appeal is reflected in the opinion.
outcome.appellateChange: n/a (trial-level decision; no appeal in opinion)
